trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied model repo may be imported as executable code: PrivacyFilterTorchPipeline.__init__ decides (defaulting to yes) and forwards that flag to AutoTokenizer/AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained for whatever name the substring router accepted as a privacy-filter model.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the privacy-filter model loading path; this is the only place in the pinned tree that enables remote code, it is a public constructor keyword with a True default, and it is the parameter a reader of the summary would go straight to.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ModelLoader only forwards kwargs the caller passes explicitly, so trust_remote_code=True there is the documented transformers opt-in and the caller's own decision, not something an untrusted model id can trigger.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: All three privacy-filter families ship custom modeling code and genuinely need remote code enabled (openai/privacy-filter, OpenMed/privacy-filter-nemotron, OpenMed/privacy-filter-multilingual); denying it outright makes the documented family unloadable and breaks the family-aware MLX-to-Torch substitution that tests/unit/test_privacy_filter_routing.py asserts.

O6_input_shapes: MLX-only ids that get substituted before loading (OpenMed/privacy-filter-*-mlx, -mlx-8bit)
local filesystem directory of an artifact whose config.json/openmed-mlx.json identifies a privacy-filter family
any third-party repo whose id merely contains the substring 'privacy-filter' (e.g. someone/privacy-filter-x) - the shape the substring router wrongly trusts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: extract_pii()/deidentify() are library entry points that never run validate_model_name, so a model id goes straight from the caller to the privacy-filter dispatcher
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: library callers are already trusted code; only the HTTP service is the untrusted boundary, and the schemas validate there
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the dispatcher call, one package from the torch sink

O8_uncovered_routes.route: the documented public helper create_privacy_filter_pipeline(model_name) builds the sink directly and accepts any repo id
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is an internal backend-selection helper linked from the docs, not a request-facing API
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one call layer above the torch sink, same package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: convert_weights(model_id) loads an arbitrary HF repo for MLX export and could gain trust_remote_code=True
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the OPF/privacy-filter architecture needs custom modeling code, so a maintainer adding an MLX-conversion path for it would plausibly enable remote code to make conversion work

O8b_injection_room.sibling: coreml convert(model_id) loads an arbitrary HF repo the same way
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same pressure as MLX conversion: privacy-filter family members only load when their custom code is importable

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the generic HF pipeline factory accepts and forwards trust_remote_code from kwargs for any model id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: users register new fine-tunes by id; forwarding the flag is the shortest way to make a custom-architecture fine-tune load

O9_family: CWE-94 code injection: remote code execution by importing modelling code from an untrusted model repo

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend; optional extras hf / service / mlx / coreml; pytest with testpaths=tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/test_privacy_filter_routing.py (routing + substitution), tests/unit/test_pii.py:259-320 (dispatcher routing), tests/unit/mlx/test_privacy_filter_mlx.py (MLX family, requires mlx); no test at the pinned commit mentions trust_remote_code or an allowlist

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Flip the default to trust_remote_code=False (or drop the keyword) in PrivacyFilterTorchPipeline and stop, which keeps the sink closed for the reported example but makes every documented privacy-filter family unloadable.

unverified: The fix diff file contains only the merge-commit header (98724f65df98d7518b9006e6356740aa36c2f224, 'Merge pull request #59 from maziyarpanahi/security/model-allowlist') and no hunks, so the exact changed lines and the metadata counts (c_fix_sites=8, c_site_files=4, c_same_check_sites=2) could not be read. fix_sites are the pinned-commit trust-decision points reconstructed from the code; the branch name implies a new is_trusted_for_remote_code allowlist helper that does not exist at the pinned commit (grep finds it nowhere).
